claimed_invariant: For the legacy sequence engine, one ordered source event stream creates one accepted LifeLine variation history and one ordered collection of concrete graphical elements. Every spacing, note anchor, activation segment, group membership, frame, external arrow, divider, and canvas query reads those same objects. Horizontal constraints are solved once, then the maximum left and right deficits of all concrete elements translate and extend that shared solution exactly once.
causal_divergence: Rust materializes lifecycle acceptance twice and horizontal geometry in several scans. The two lifecycle projections disagree on equal-ordinate rejection, return ownership, self messages, group-end attachment, and page boundaries. The early note reservation and later note-only missing-space pass double-count some notes while omitting group headers and external arrows. Frames and dividers are then rebuilt after translation from different aggregates. This explains the one-pixel left-note shifts, negative grouped-frame origins, five-to-fourteen-pixel lifecycle/page shifts, shortened external arrows, and canvas/frame width disagreements.
